title: How Does a Tow Truck Lift a Car?
sources: Tow Truck Association basics: how towing works
National Highway Traffic Safety Administration: vehicle safety

beats.say: This is me! I'm a tow truck. Do you know how I lift a whole car?
Hi! I'm Bolt, the little tow truck. Let's roll!
I have a strong arm on my back called a boom. A long cable hangs down with a yellow hook.
The hook holds the front of the car, and my boom lifts it up, up, up.
Then I carry the car to the garage, so it can get fixed and go vroom again! Beep, beep, here I come!
Can you lift your arms up like a tow truck boom? Up, up! Be kind and wave hello! See you in Tiny Truck Town!

title: How Does a Street Sweeper Clean the Road?
sources: American Public Works Association: street sweeping
U.S. EPA: keeping streets and storm drains clean

beats.say: Swish, swish! Which truck has brushes that sweep the street?
Hi! I'm Bolt, the little tow truck. Let's roll!
A street sweeper has round brushes underneath that spin and spin to sweep up dirt and leaves. Some sweepers have a brush on the side too, to clean along the curb.
It sprays a little water too, so the dust does not fly up into the air.
Then it scoops everything into a big box inside. A clean street for everyone!
Can you pretend to sweep with a broom? Swish, swish! Swish, swish, all clean! Be kind and wave hello! See you in Tiny Truck Town!

title: Forklifts Lift Heavy Boxes Way Up High!
sources: OSHA: powered industrial trucks (forklifts)
Industrial Truck Association: forklift basics

beats.say: Who can lift a stack of heavy boxes way up high? Let's find out!
Hi! I'm Bolt, the little tow truck. Let's roll!
A forklift has two long flat arms called forks. They slide right under the boxes.
Then the forks go up, up, up, to put the boxes on a tall shelf.
A heavy weight on the back keeps the forklift steady, so it will not tip. Forklifts work in big warehouses, where lots and lots of boxes are stored.
Can you hold out two fingers like forks and lift them up? Up, up! Be kind and wave hello! See you in Tiny Truck Town!

title: Why Is the Road Roller So Heavy?
sources: Federal Highway Administration: asphalt pavement construction
National Asphalt Pavement Association

beats.say: This truck has no front wheels. It has a giant drum! What does it do?
Hi! I'm Bolt, the little tow truck. Let's roll!
A road roller is super heavy. Its big round drum presses new road flat and smooth.
It rolls slowly back and forth, back and forth, until the road is ready.
Water sprays on the drum, so the warm, sticky road does not stick to it. Then the new road is ready for cars, bikes and buses!
Can you roll your hands like a big drum? Roll, roll, roll! Smooth! Be kind and wave hello! See you in Tiny Truck Town!

title: Why Is It Called a Cherry Picker?
sources: OSHA: aerial lifts
Agricultural history: orchard ladders and lifts

beats.say: This truck has a bucket that goes way up high. Can you guess its funny name?
Hi! I'm Bolt, the little tow truck. Let's roll!
It's called a cherry picker! Long ago, lifts like this helped farmers pick fruit from tall trees.
Today, a worker rides up in the bucket to fix tall streetlights and wires.
The long arm bends and stretches, so the bucket can reach just the right spot. The worker wears a safety belt clipped to the bucket.
Can you stretch up tall, like you're picking cherries? Reach, reach! Up we go! Be kind and wave hello! See you in Tiny Truck Town!

title: Monster Truck Tires Are as Tall as a Grown-Up!
sources: Monster truck sport technical specifications: 66-inch tires
Science museum guides: shock absorbers

beats.say: Look at these giant tires! How big are monster truck tires?
Hi! I'm Bolt, the little tow truck. Let's roll!
Monster truck tires are huge. One tire can be as tall as a grown-up! That's bigger than me!
Big bouncy springs called shocks help the truck land softly after a jump. Squish, then bounce!
Monster trucks put on shows, with jumps and big wheelies for the crowd. The drivers wear helmets and seat belts, and the trucks are built extra strong.
Can you bounce like a monster truck? Boing, boing! Be kind and wave hello! See you in Tiny Truck Town!

title: Why Does the Ice Cream Truck Play Music?
sources: Food truck basics: refrigeration and freezers
Community history of ice cream trucks

beats.say: Do you hear a happy song? Which truck plays music as it drives?
Hi! I'm Bolt, the little tow truck. Let's roll!
The ice cream truck! It plays a song so everyone knows it's coming down the street.
Inside, a big freezer keeps the ice cream cold and frosty, so it doesn't melt. Brrr! It's like a freezer on wheels.
A grown-up can help you buy a treat from the little window. Wait on the sidewalk, and look both ways with your grown-up.
What's your favorite ice cream flavor? Mine is strawberry! Be kind and wave hello! See you in Tiny Truck Town!

title: Why Is the Mail Truck Steering Wheel on the Right?
sources: U.S. Postal Service: history of delivery vehicles
Smithsonian National Postal Museum

beats.say: This mail truck's steering wheel is on the other side. Do you know why?
Hi! I'm Bolt, the little tow truck. Let's roll!
A mail truck carries letters and packages to houses all over town.
Many mail trucks have the steering wheel on the right side, close to the mailboxes. Isn't that clever?
That way, the mail carrier can reach out and put the mail right in the mailbox! Mail carriers deliver letters in sunshine, rain and even snow.
Can you pretend to put a letter in a mailbox? Drop! Here's a letter for you! Be kind and wave hello! See you in Tiny Truck Town!

title: How Many Cars Can a Car Carrier Carry?
sources: Trucking industry guides: car haulers
Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration

beats.say: This truck carries cars on top of cars! How many can it carry?
Hi! I'm Bolt, the little tow truck. Let's roll!
A car carrier has two floors, one on top and one on the bottom. It's like a parking garage on wheels!
Some car carriers can carry up to ten cars at once!
It brings brand-new cars from the factory to the car stores. Ramps help the cars drive on and off. The top floor can tilt down, like a ramp, too.
Let's count the cars! One, two, three, four, five, six, seven! Be kind and wave hello! See you in Tiny Truck Town!

title: How Does a Snowplow Clear the Road?
sources: Federal Highway Administration: snow and ice control
American Public Works Association: winter maintenance

beats.say: Brrr! The road is covered in snow. Which truck can clear it?
Hi! I'm Bolt, the little tow truck. Let's roll!
A snowplow has a giant curved blade in front. It pushes snow off to the side of the road.
In the back, it spreads salt and sand, so the road is not slippery. Salt helps melt the ice.
Snowplows often work at night, so roads are ready in the morning. Bright flashing lights help everyone see the plow coming.
Can you push like a snowplow? Push, push, push! Whoosh! Be kind and wave hello! See you in Tiny Truck Town!

title: Helicopters Can Fly Backward!
sources: NASA Glenn Research Center: how helicopters fly
FAA Helicopter Flying Handbook

beats.say: Whirr, whirr! Which flying machine can stay still in the sky?
Hi! I'm Bolt, the little tow truck. Let's roll!
A helicopter has long blades on top called a rotor. They spin super fast to lift it up.
A helicopter can go straight up, hover in one spot, and even fly backward! Wow!
The little rotor on the tail keeps it from spinning around and around. Helicopters can land in small places, like the top of a tall building.
Can you spin your arm like a rotor? Whirr, whirr! Lift off! Be kind and wave hello! See you in Tiny Truck Town!

title: Why Are Race Cars So Low?
sources: Motorsport engineering guides: downforce and grip
Science museum guides: aerodynamics

beats.say: Zoom! Race cars sit really low, close to the road. Why?
Hi! I'm Bolt, the little tow truck. Let's roll!
Being low and wide helps a race car hold the road tight when it turns.
The wing on the back pushes the car down, so the tires grip the track. Race cars use smooth tires called slicks on dry tracks.
At a pit stop, a team can change all four tires in just a few seconds! Zip, zip, zip! Then the car zooms back onto the track.
Can you go zoom in place? Ready, set, go! Be kind and wave hello! See you in Tiny Truck Town!

title: Where Does the Recycling Truck Go?
sources: U.S. EPA: recycling basics
Local public works recycling guides

beats.say: Bottles, cans and paper! Which truck takes them away?
Hi! I'm Bolt, the little tow truck. Let's roll!
The recycling truck! It picks up bottles, cans and paper from blue bins. Some recycling trucks have a robot arm that lifts the bin and tips it in.
It takes them to the recycling center, where they get sorted. Paper goes with paper, and cans go with cans.
Then they are made into brand-new things, like new paper and new cans! Recycling helps keep our planet clean and green.
Can you sort with me? Paper here, cans there! Good job! Be kind and wave hello! See you in Tiny Truck Town!

title: What Happens Inside a Car Wash?
sources: International Carwash Association: how car washes work
U.S. EPA: water reuse at car washes

beats.say: Splish, splash! Where do cars go to get clean and shiny?
Hi! I'm Bolt, the little tow truck. Let's roll!
The car wash! First, soapy bubbles cover the car from top to bottom. So many bubbles! Pop, pop!
Big soft brushes spin around and scrub away the dirt. Swish, swish, around and around.
Then water rinses the soap off. Many car washes clean and reuse their water! Last, warm air blows the car dry. Shiny and clean!
Can you pretend to scrub like a car wash brush? Scrub, scrub! Scrub-a-dub-dub! Be kind and wave hello! See you in Tiny Truck Town!

title: What Do Traffic Light Colors Mean?
sources: U.S. Department of Transportation: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices
NHTSA: pedestrian safety for kids

beats.say: Red, yellow, green! What does each traffic light color mean?
Hi! I'm Bolt, the little tow truck. Let's roll!
Red means stop. On most traffic lights, red is at the very top. Cars stop and wait. Stop!
Yellow means slow down. The light will be red very soon. Cars get ready to stop. Slow, slow, slow.
Green means go! Cars can drive when the light is green. People walking wait for the walking light before they cross.
Let's play! Red light, stop! Green light, go! Always cross with a grown-up. Be kind and wave hello! See you in Tiny Truck Town!

title: How Does a Big Airplane Back Up?
sources: FAA: airport ground operations
Airport ground support equipment guides

beats.say: Big airplanes don't back up by themselves at the gate. So who helps?
Hi! I'm Bolt, the little tow truck. Let's roll!
A little tug! It's low and flat, so it fits right under the airplane's nose. Tugs are small, but they are super strong.
A strong bar connects the tug to the airplane's front wheel.
Then the tug pushes the giant airplane backward, away from the gate. Small but mighty! Once the plane is out, it can drive to the runway by itself.
Can you push like a tug? Push, push! Be kind and wave hello! See you in Tiny Truck Town!
